:::writing{variant="social_post" id="58317"}
Exactly one year ago, I walked into this house and started over.

A year later, I'm realizing healing doesn't always happen in the big, dramatic moments. Sometimes it shows up in the smallest milestones.

Last week was the first time I recharged my toothbrush.

Yesterday was the first time I finally hung a mirror in my bedroom.

A few days ago was the first time I started reading my Bible in the mornings again.

Recently was the first time I started working out again, something that used to bring me so much joy.

Those things may seem insignificant to someone else, but to me, they're proof that I'm coming back to life.

Leaving a narcissistic, emotionally abusive relationship that everyone thought looked perfectly fine from the outside does more damage than most people will ever understand. It feels like a death.

The death of the life you thought you'd have.

The death of what you believed was forever.

The death of the version of yourself that slowly disappeared while trying to survive.

But I've realized something.

I haven't been mourning.

I've been shedding.

Shedding everything that was never meant for me so God could rebuild the woman He created me to be.

This past year has been filled with healing, grace, and blessings I never could have imagined.

I've been given the gift of a man who has been unbelievably gentle, patient, and steady as I've navigated this unfamiliar season of becoming myself again. He has loved me through the healing instead of rushing it.

I've watched my son continue to become one of the greatest men I know. He has been patient, encouraging, and endlessly supportive. He will forever be my greatest accomplishment, my biggest earthly blessing, and one of God's greatest gifts in my life.

I've been surrounded by parents and family who never stopped believing in me. Friends, both old and new, who have shown up in different ways throughout this journey. Some close. Some from a distance. Every single one serving a purpose.

But above all else, one thing has never failed me.

God.

When everything else felt uncertain, His love never wavered. He never left my side. He carried me when I couldn't carry myself, and He continues to write a story that is far more beautiful than anything I could have planned.

If this past year has taught me anything, it's this:

God doesn't just restore what was lost.

He creates something even more beautiful from the ashes.

Here's to the woman I left behind.

Here's to the woman I'm becoming.

And here's to the year ahead, filled with more faith, more healing, more joy, more purpose, and more miracles than I can even imagine.

My prayer is that people never see me.

I pray they see God's glory through the mess He redeemed.

Because with Him, absolutely nothing is impossible. 🤍
:::
